The test image shows corn leaves with prominent yellow-white streaks running along the length of the leaf, following the veins. This is a leaf symptom at what appears to be a tasseling/silking stage.

The streaking pattern (alternating green and pale/white bands along veins) is highly characteristic of viral diseases. Top candidates: Maize_Streak_Virus, Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus, Stewart_S_Disease.

Let me view one reference image for Maize_Streak_Virus to confirm.

The reference image for Maize_Streak_Virus shows fine, dense yellow streaks along veins. The test image shows broader, more prominent pale/white streaks running the full length of leaves.

Comparing features:
- Test image: broad white/pale cream elongated streaks parallel to leaf veins, running full leaf length, plant at tasseling stage, red soil (African context)
- Maize_Streak_Virus reference: finer yellow streaking along veins — somewhat different but same fundamental pattern
- Stewart's Disease: "bleached leaf streaks running the length of the leaf" — also matches the broad pale streaks
- Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus: narrow light green/yellow streaks — less consistent with the broad pale streaks shown

The broad pale/white stripes running full length of the leaf in the test image, combined with the context (red laterite soil typical of sub-Saharan Africa where MSV is endemic), point most strongly to Maize_Streak_Virus. The slightly coarser streak pattern vs. the reference could be a severity/stage difference.
